title: Grateful Dead Live at Monterey Fairgrounds on 1967-06-18
lineage: SBD > MR > Cass > DAT > ZA2 > CD

ai_review.summary: Historic 1967 Monterey Pop set with raw energy and iconic Viola Lee Blues; soundboard capture is generally good despite occasional muddiness.
ai_review.review: The recording captures the Grateful Dead’s early‑Monterey Pop performance, highlighted by a blazing Viola Lee Blues, driving Cold Rain and Snow, and the quirky Caution (Do Not Step On The Tracks). While the soundboard source provides a listenable mix, reviewers note occasional muddy sections—especially on Jerry’s solos—and inserted interview clips that make the tape feel a bit jumbled. Overall the show is praised for its historic significance and high‑octane playing.

ai_rating.rationale: The majority of reviews are 4–5 stars, praising the performance and historical value; only one low rating cites source issues. Weighted toward show quality (70%) with solid but imperfect recording quality yields a strong overall rating.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Generally clear soundboard mix, but occasional muddyness on Jerry’s solos and brief sound‑system problems; interview excerpts are inserted, making the tape feel jumbled for some listeners.

standout_songs: Caution (Do Not Step On The Tracks)
show_quality.setlist_flow: Early Monterey Pop slot; raw, high‑energy set that feels extemporaneous and historically pivotal despite a less tight overall performance compared to later shows.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Garcia’s guitar is described as amazing and blazing, though his solos sometimes sound muddy due to recording issues.
band_member_comments.Phil: Phil was reportedly upset about the forced filming release forms; no specific musical commentary.
